france24fr.description: L'Espagne a remporté son duel face à l'Autriche en 16es de finale de Coupe du monde grâce à un doublé d'Oyarzabal et un but de Porro (3-0). Elle défiera au prochain tour le vainqueur de Portugal - Croatie.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les Bleus de retour à l'entraînement avant le match contre le Paraguay
france24fr.description: Les Bleus sont de retour à l'entraînement après leur victoire contre la Suède, 3-0. Ils affronteront le Paraguay à Philadelphie le 4 juillet.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : renversé par la Belgique malgré deux buts d'avance, le Sénégal ne verra pas les 8e
france24fr.description: Le Sénégal est éliminé de la Coupe du monde 2026 après un match renversant contre la Belgique ce mercredi. Les Lions de la Teranga menait par 2 buts à zéro avant de subir une remontada dans les dernières minutes. Au Sénégal c'est la colère et la frustration.

france24fr.title: Patrick Bruel visé par trois nouvelles plaintes pour violences sexuelles
france24fr.description: D'après Mediapart, deux plaintes pour viol et une pour agression sexuelle sur mineure ont été déposées contre la star française Patrick Bruel. Parmi les trois actions judiciaires, l'une concerne des faits qui ne sont pas prescrits.

france24fr.title: L'opposition congolaise a-t-elle armé des manifestants à Kinshasa ?
france24fr.description: En République Démocratique du Congo, de fausses informations sont nées en marge de la contestation contre la réforme constitutionnelle visant à permettre au président Tshisekedi de se représenter. Certains internautes affirment que l'opposition aurait armé des manifestants à Kinshasa, sur la base d'une prétendue interview donnée sur France24. Une vidéo fausse, qui usurpe l'identité de France24. Jules Boiteau dans Info Intox.

france24fr.title: Le rêve américain existe-t-il encore ?
france24fr.description: Ce samedi 4 juillet, les États-Unis célèbrent les 250 ans de leur Déclaration d'indépendance. L'histoire d'une ancienne colonie devenue la première puissance mondiale, aujourd'hui dirigée par Donald Trump. Les commémorations de cet acte fondateur font polémique, le président américain est accusé d’instrumentaliser l’événement.

france24fr.title: RDC : le système de la prédation minière
france24fr.description: Selon le rapport de l'ONU rendu début juin, en RDC, la contrebande d'or venu d'Ituri vers l'Ouganda est en forte progression. Les auteurs du document sont parvenus à cette conclusion après avoir constaté de nombreuses incohérences dans les niveaux de production et d'exportation annoncés pour 2025. Les explications avec Pierre Jacquemo, ancien diplomate en poste notamment au Sénégal, en Algérie, au Burkina, au Cameroun, au Ghana et en RDC, expert à la Fondation Jean Jaurès.

france24fr.title: Espagne - Autriche : la Roja  se qualifie facilement pour les 8es de finale
france24fr.description: Favori annoncé de la Coupe du monde, l'Espagne a rendez-vous jeudi avec l'Autriche en 16es de finale. Qui de la Roja ou de das Team se qualifiera pour le tour suivant ? Une rencontre à suivre en direct grâce à au live commenté animé par nos confrères de RFI.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Pape Gueye annonce une pause dans sa carrière avec l'équipe du Sénégal
france24fr.description: Une annonce assez surprenante de Pape Gueye dans la nuit, quelques heures après l’élimination du Sénégal en 16e de finale du Mondial 2026. Dans une story sur Instagram, le joueur sénégalais a indiqué qu'il fera une pause sur la sélection nationale, tant que le staff technique actuellement dirigé par Pape Thiaw sera maintenu à la tête de l’équipe.

france24fr.title: France : "Le peuple se soulève quand il n'a pas de pain, mais aussi quand il est mauvais"
france24fr.description:
C'est une émission qui va vous donner envie de manger du pain 🍞: Steven Kaplan, historien américain et spécialiste du pain, revient avec nous sur cet aliment à la fois symbole politique, religieux et emblème de la France, aujourd'hui beaucoup moins présent sur nos tables.
 
Retrouvez son interview intégrale dans l'émission "Avec Judith", diffusée ce samedi à midi sur le site de France 24.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : au Sénégal, le coach Pape Thiaw cible des critiques après l’élimination des Lions
france24fr.description: Au lendemain de l’élimination du Sénégal du Mondial 2026, Pape Thiaw essuie de vives critiques. Les Lions ont laissé échapper une avance de 2-0 face à la Belgique dans les dernières minutes du match. Une défaite jugée cruelle et injuste par de nombreux Sénégalais.

france24fr.title: Cameroun : le gouvernement sort du silence sur l'affaire des décrets
france24fr.description:
🇨🇲 Au Cameroun, le gouvernement sort du silence sur l'affaire des décrets. Le mois dernier, un individu s'est rendu dans les locaux de la radio nationale à Yaoundé, et y a déposé un pli fermé contenant deux prétendus décrets présidentiels portant les nominations d'un vice-président de la République et d’un nouveau gouvernement.
 
Les documents officiels, n'avaient finalement pas été diffusés après vérification. Les précisions de notre correspondant à Yaoundé, Marcel Amoko.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027: La question des ralliements, le RN suspendu à la décision de la cour d'appel
france24fr.description: A moins d’un an de la présidentielle, la politique entre dans le temps des calculs. Laurent Wauquiez, chef des Républicains à l’Assemblée nationale, n’exclut plus un rapprochement avec Edouard Philippe, marquant ainsi une rupture avec Bruno Retailleau. A gauche, en revanche le désordre règne : malgré les appels au rassemblement, les divisions l’emportent. Du côté du RN, la cour d’appel va rendre sa décision avec à la clé la possibilité ou non pour Marine Le Pen de se présenter en 2027.

france24fr.title: Régularisation des sans-papiers en Espagne : près de 1,2 million de demandes ont été déposées
france24fr.description: L'Espagne a reçu près de 1,2 million de demandes de régularisation entre mi-avril et le 30 juin. Deux tiers des étrangers en situation irrégulière ayant déposé un dossier sont originaires d'Amérique latine, selon des chiffres communiqués jeudi par le gouvernement socialiste de Pedro Sanchez.

france24fr.title: France : incendies majeurs dans le sud du pays
france24fr.description: Des centaines de pompiers luttent jeudi dans le Sud contre des incendies attisés par le vent, la sécheresse et la chaleur, le plus important dans l'Aude, mais aussi au nord de Marseille, où le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu est arrivé pour présider une nouvelle cellule interministérielle de crise.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : la Russie au défi du brouillage de Starlink
france24fr.description: Des images montreraient la destruction, par les forces ukrainiennes, d'un système russe visant à brouiller les signaux Starlink, qui serait actuellement déployé sur le front. Ce réseau, particulièrement difficile à neutraliser, est devenu crucial pour fournir un accès à Internet à haut débit à l'Ukraine.

france24fr.title: La condamnation de Dany Leprince annulée dans un rebondissement rarissime
france24fr.description: Coup de tonnerre dans l'affaire Dany Leprince. L’homme avait été condamné à la prison à perpétuité en 1997 pour un quadruple meurtre dans la Sarthe. Il a déjà passé 18 ans derrière les barreaux, mais ce matin la Cour de révision a annulé sa condamnation... une décision rarissime. Un nouveau procès aura donc lieu.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 Live: Drei Erkenntnisse aus Spaniens Sieg gegen Österreich
spiegel.description: Vielleicht haben wir den künftigen Weltmeister gesehen. Marc Cucurella ist einer der besten Außenverteidiger der Welt. Für Österreich hätte es noch schlimmer kommen können. Die Partie aus Los Angeles im Liveticker.

spiegel.title: Hantavirus: WHO erklärt tödlichen Ausbruch auf einem Kreuzfahrtschiff für beendet
spiegel.description: Die letzte Kontaktperson, die dem Hantavirus-Ausbruch ausgesetzt war, ist negativ getestet worden. Insgesamt sind an dem Ausbruch auf einem Kreuzfahrtschiff drei Personen gestorben.

spiegel.title: Mount Everest: Indien will 30 Jahre alte Leiche bergen
spiegel.description: Er gilt für Bergsteiger als Wegmarke. Und als Mahnung: Seit 30 Jahren liegt der Leichnam eines Inders mit grünen Schuhen am Mount Everest. Nun hat soll »Green Boots« geborgen werden – doch der Aufwand ist enorm.

spiegel.title: Reformpaket: Opposition und Verbände kritisieren Beschlüsse – Merz und Klingbeil verteidigen es
spiegel.description: Das Reformpaket der Koalition stößt auf teils heftige Kritik: Besonders die Steuerpläne und die Krankschreibungspflicht ab dem ersten Tag werden bemängelt. SPD-Chef Lars Klingbeil weicht erste Ankündigungen wieder auf.

spiegel.title: Washington: Ex-Olympiasportler David Hearn wegen Vandalismus am Reflecting Pool angeklagt
spiegel.description: Der Reflecting Pool in Washington sollte nach großer Renovierung blau statt grün erstrahlen. Daraus wurde nichts, das Wasser ist voller Algen. Trump wälzt die Schuld auf andere ab, nun droht die Härte des Gesetzes.

spiegel.title: Ifo-Chef Clemens Fuest lobt das Reformpaket der Bundesregierung
spiegel.description: Als Schritt in die richtige Richtung lobt Clemens Fuest die Regierungsbeschlüsse. Der Chef des Ifo-Instituts erklärt, warum er ein Verbot von Wohnungsenteignungen unterstützt und wo er die größte Schwäche des Pakets sieht.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Selenskyj fordert eigene Patriot-Produktion
spiegel.description: Um Angriffe wie die der vergangenen Nacht abzuwehren, braucht die Ukraine Patriot-Systeme. Doch die sind rar. Für eine bessere Flugabwehr will Präsident Selenskyj nun eine eigene Produktionsstätte – und die US-Lizenz.

spiegel.title: Hollywood: Franka Potentes Freunde sind arbeitslos
spiegel.description: Mit 40 noch mal zurück zu den Eltern ziehen: Für manche Schauspieler-Freunde von Franka Potente ist das Realität. Sie selbst kann sich das Leben in Hollywood aber noch leisten.

spiegel.title: Albanien: Festnahmen bei »Flamingo-Protesten« in Tirana
spiegel.description: In Tirana geraten Demonstranten und Polizisten aneinander. Die Wut geht längst über ein Luxus-Bauprojekt hinaus, im Widerstand gegen die Regierung gibt es Festnahmen und Verletzte.

spiegel.title: Julian Reichelt: Rechts-außen-Portal gewinnt an Einfluss - Podcast Firewall
spiegel.description: Als Chefredakteur von bild.de startete er 2015 eine Refugees-welcome-Kampagne. Heute hetzt Julian Reichelt mit »Nius« gegen Migranten. Trotzdem gewinnt das Portal an Einfluss – sogar in der politischen Mitte.

spiegel.title: Israel: Warum Benjamin Netanyahu als Favorit in den Wahlkampf zieht
spiegel.description: Benjamin Netanyahu ist militärisch gescheitert, diplomatisch isoliert und wird nun auch noch von US-Präsident Donald Trump brüskiert. Warum er trotzdem weiter regieren könnte.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump bezeichnet Deutschlands Nato-Ausgaben als »lächerlich«
spiegel.description: Donald Trump ist unzufrieden mit den Verteidigungsausgaben seiner Nato-Partner. Besonders Deutschland kommt in einem Post auf Truth Social schlecht weg. Die Äußerungen kommen kurz vor dem wichtigen Nato-Gipfel.

spiegel.title: Krankschreibungen: Warum Atteste ab dem ersten Tag teuer und wirkungslos sind
spiegel.description: Wer krank wird, braucht künftig sofort ein Attest. Das ist teuer für die Versicherten und schafft neue Probleme.

spiegel.title: Stade: Fatih Khan G. wollte sich offenbar nach der Tat das Leben nehmen
spiegel.description: Es gibt neue Details über die Bluttat von Stade: Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen schickte der mutmaßliche Täter offenbar seine Frau aus dem Raum, in dem er tötete. Und nun rückt auch die Fahrerin seines Fluchtwagens in den Blick.

spiegel.title: Basteltipps für die Ferien: Das wird ein Super-Sommer
spiegel.description: Was man aus Chipsdosen und Muschelfunden machen kann? Viele kreative Dinge. Hier sind fünf Bastelideen für die großen Ferien. Das Beste: Sie kosten fast nichts.

spiegel.title: Wien: Heinz-Christian Strache in Untreue-Prozess freigesprochen
spiegel.description: Das Landesgericht Wien hat den ehemaligen Vizekanzler Österreichs, Heinz-Christian Strache, vom Vorwurf der Untreue entlastet. Laut Anklage wollte er sich unrechtmäßig eine Versicherungssumme auszahlen lassen.

spiegel.title: »The Piano Tuner« mit Dustin Hoffman: Bei diesem Ganovenfilm stimmt nicht nur das Klavier
spiegel.description: Ein hochbegabter junger Mann lässt sich mit einer Bande von Panzerknackern ein, weil sein absolutes Gehör auch bei Safeschlössern ganz nützlich ist. »The Piano Tuner« ist ein hinreißender Kinospaß.

spiegel.title: »Shrek 5« kommt erst 2027 ins Kino. Fans ärgern sich schon jetzt
spiegel.description: Als Prinzessin entschied sich die menschliche Fiona der Liebe willen für eine permanente Erscheinung als grüner Oger. Ein neuer Trailer zum fünften Film zeigt eine vermeintlich optimierte Version von ihr – zum Unmut im Netz.

observador.title: Trabalho à tarefa. Médicos querem intervenção do TC
observador.description: Associação de Médicos Prestadores de Serviços entende que o diploma (uma das leis-bandeira do Governo) viola vários artigos da Constituição. PS vai esperar pela portaria para decidir.

observador.title: 22h. Contagem decrescente para jogo Portugal x Croácia
observador.description: Os adeptos concentram-se na capital para assistir a este jogo dos 16 avos de final. Ainda, já há calendário para a próxima temporada da I Liga portuguesa.

observador.title: Hola, qué tal, Portugal? Estamos à vossa espera!
observador.description: Espanha venceu confortavelmente a Áustria por 3-0, dois golos de Oyarzabal e Porro. Num jogo em que teve 65% posse de bola, fez 23 remates, mais de 600 passes e 9-0 em cantos. Segue-se Portugal?

observador.title: "O Eusébio cantava o hino da Croácia"
observador.description: Depois de conquistar a Europa, Eusébio aventurou-se na América e o melhor momento aconteceu no Canadá. Jogou numa equipa de croatas, foi campeão e em Toronto garantem que nunca será esquecido.

observador.title: Carneiro vs AD. Há casas vazias, mas não por eleitoralismo
observador.description: Há casas do PRR vazias há ano e meio, como diz o PS, mas autarcas socialistas apontam à burocracia. Governo diz que Carneiro expôs localização confidencial de abrigo para vítimas de violência.

observador.title: Oyarzabal, um verdadeiro Robin para o Batman de Yamal
observador.description: Num dia em que Lamine Yamal apareceu em LA com um Batman ao pescoço, Oyarzabal voltou a mostrar que é um verdadeiro Robin e liderou a vitória de Espanha contra a Áustria rumo aos oitavos (2-0).

observador.title: PS: só há desequilíbrio "se o Governo incumpriu a lei"
observador.description: "Ou o PSD veio tentar alarmar os portugueses mentindo" ou veio assumir que o Governo não cumpriu a lei, lançou Mendonça Mendes, depois de o PSD apontar para custo de 300 milhões de euros da medida.

observador.title: Sines. BE preocupado com impacto do negócio Galp-Moeve
observador.description: Fabian Figueiredo defendeu que o acordo entre as duas empresas representa a perda do "controlo do único ativo nacional de refinação", que assegura cerca de 90% dos combustíveis consumidos em Portugal.

observador.title: Roupa funcional, upcycling e tricô online com o Bloom
observador.description: Jovens do Bloom apostam na reutilização, e.p. ate'lye faz colab com a Salsa e Ministra assiste a showcase: "Queremos criar condições para que a moda possa atrair mais investimento privado".

observador.title: 21h. Calor. IPMA prevê quadro meteorológico complexo
observador.description: As próximas duas noites vão ser muito quentes. e com previsões de muito vento. Ainda, A Câmara Municipal de Lisboa decidiu fechar os espaços florestais na sequência da situação de alerta.

observador.title: 63 afogamentos de crianças e jovens entre 2000 e 2024
observador.description: GNR e APSI lançam campanha na próxima semana após dados alarmantes: mortalidade subiu no pós-pandemia e mantém-se acima do mínimo histórico.

observador.title: Trump quer travar "assassínios sem sentido" na Ucrânia
observador.description: EUA dizem que Trump quer acabar com os "assassínios sem sentido" na Ucrânia. Rússia lançou cerca de 500 drones e 70 mísseis balísticos, a maioria sobre Kiev, com 21 mortos.

observador.title: Sebastião Bugalho: O refresco milagroso da política
observador.description: O "Messias" da AD: um Bugalho tão bom que faz o resto do Governo parecer amador. Um "cocktail de assinatura" para animar quem já desistiu da política e o manual de sobrevivência do Estado-avozinha.

observador.title: Brasil critica sanções dos EUA a suspeitos do PCC
observador.description: Washington sancionou dois brasileiros e três empresas por ligação ao PCC. Brasília rejeita as medidas e alerta para riscos de restrições a instituições financeiras brasileiras.

observador.title: Crise de combustível na península da Crimeia é "alarmante"
observador.description: A crise de combustível na Crimeia anexada provocou uma escalada nos preços da gasolina. Dados oficiais da agência federal russa de estatísticas revelam uma subida vertiginosa de 30% numa semana.

observador.title: Rússia leva a cabo um dos ataques mais mortíferos na Ucrânia
observador.description: A capital da Ucrânia foi atingida pelo mais massivo ataque aéreo desde o início da invasão. Várias áreas residenciais foram atingidas. Pelo menos 23 pessoas morreram e 100 ficaram feridas.

observador.title: "Putin está a tentar escalar o conflito"
observador.description: Ana Cavalieri analisa o dilema do líder russo: negociar em termos desfavoráveis ou escalar o conflito com ataques a civis para tornar o custo da guerra cada vez mais "doloroso" para a Ucrânia.

observador.title: 20h. Meios reforçados no incêndio em Vouzela
observador.description: Estão agora no terreno 450 operacionais acompanhados de oito viaturas. Ainda, a escritora Lídia Jorge é a vencedora do Prémio Camões deste ano.

elpais.title: España - Austria: Mundial 2026, en directo | De la Fuente: “Los grandes equipos aparecen cuando se les necesita”
elpais.description: El doblete de Oyarzabal y el tanto de Pedro Porro consuman el convincente triunfo de la Selección en Los Ángeles | El rival en la siguiente ronda saldrá del Portugal-Croacia de esta madrugada

elpais.title: Moreno cede y pacta un gobierno de coalición con Vox
elpais.description: Los ultras entran en el Ejecutivo andaluz con una vicepresidencia de Turismo, desregulación, justicia y administración local

elpais.title: El juez Pedraz imputa a la directora de la Guardia Civil y a su número dos en el ‘caso Leire’
elpais.description: El magistrado acoge la petición de la Fiscalía Anticorrupción y los cita el próximo 16 de julio por delitos de prevaricación y obstrucción a la justicia

elpais.title: “Al amigo Feu, de Sorolla”: el cuadro perdido en Sevilla vuelve a casa entre incógnitas
elpais.description: El lienzo de 1919, abandonado por error en la calle y encontrado por un turista murciano, regresa a manos de la familia propietaria sin aclarar a quién pertenecía originalmente y cómo lo obtuvieron

elpais.title: La justicia obliga a Atresmedia a indemnizar a la socorrista del vídeo viral ‘La he liado parda’
elpais.description: La Audiencia de Madrid considera que el uso de la imagen y su voz en parodias lesionaron su honor y eleva la condena a 50.000 euros más intereses

elpais.title: La justicia busca a Vito Quiles por un bulo contra un empleado público: dijo que Yolanda Díaz le había excarcelado y enchufado
elpais.description: El agitador dijo que el hombre estuvo encarcelado por un delito grave y que Díaz logró que quedara libre y lo contrató en el Ministerio de Trabajo

elpais.title: Medio mundo al rescate de Hernán: un venezolano sale con vida de entre los escombros tras ocho días sepultado por el terremoto
elpais.description: Un centenar de personas de diez países logran salvar al hombre en una operación contrarreloj en la que todos corrieron peligro por la situación inestable del edificio

elpais.title: Un último baile mundialista para Cristiano o Modric en un partido marcado por el primer aniversario de la muerte de Diogo Jota
elpais.description: Portugal y Croacia se miden en Toronto en dieciseisavos en un choque que supondrá el adiós definitivo de la Copa del Mundo de uno de los dos mitos. El ganador se verá con España o Austria en la siguiente ronda

elpais.title: ¿Cómo están los cruces del Mundial? Consulte los rivales probables de cada selección hasta la final
elpais.description: Un interactivo de EL PAÍS muestra el cuadro actualizado después de cada partido

elpais.title: Ni jugar ni ganar: el drama de Países Bajos y Alemania
elpais.description: Había un fondo común innegociable que se ha diluido con el tiempo, que era el de atacar, ir a por la victoria hasta el extremo de que la derrota se asumía como parte irremediable del proceso. Hoy se ha impuesto el resultadismo

elpais.title: Así desciframos qué país puede ganar el Mundial
elpais.description: La herramienta elaborada por EL PAÍS combina cuatro bancos de datos para hacer cálculos de probabilidades sobre cómo se pueden comportar las selecciones de fútbol durante la competición

elpais.title: Feijóomandering, o de la ‘ingeniería electoral’
elpais.description: Al líder del PP le parecía bien la ‘ley de nietos’ hasta que cayó en la cuenta de que el PSOE también puede hacer campaña en el exterior

elpais.title: Escuela de calor
elpais.description: El ministro de Trabajo francés quiere venir a España a aprender cómo seguimos vivos y trabajando con este calorazo, pero tampoco estamos para dar lecciones

elpais.title: La Comunidad de Madrid aprueba, ahora sí, su ley del concebido no nacido
elpais.description: La Asamblea celebra una sesión extraordinaria después de que se parara la tramitación de una de las normas en las que más empeño ha puesto la presidenta por un defecto de forma

elpais.title: Migraciones ha regularizado a cerca de 11.000 personas de un total de 1,17 millones de solicitudes presentadas
elpais.description: El 52% de los expedientes ha sido admitido a trámite por el momento y un 26% de ellos se ha dado de alta en la Seguridad Social

elpais.title: Beneficiados de la ‘ley de nietos’: “La nacionalidad es una forma de entender el origen”
elpais.description: Seis descendientes de emigrantes relatan su experiencia como nuevos ciudadanos españoles desde América

elpais.title: Francia absuelve a Josu Ternera y abre la vía para su extradición inmediata a España
elpais.description: El tribunal considera que no ha quedado probado que perteneciese a ETA entre 2002 y 2005, lo que liquida su periplo judicial en este país y despeja el camino para ejecutar las euroórdenes que pesan sobre él

elpais.title: La Abogacía del Estado concluye que Kitchen buscaba robar a Bárcenas “papeles que comprometían” a Rajoy
elpais.description: Las acusaciones exponen sus alegatos finales en el juicio: “Luis Bárcenas se tenía que callar, no podía perjudicar al PP”, dice la abogada del extesorero popular

nyt.title: All New York Suffers in a Heat Wave. It’s Worse in Jamaica, Queens.
nyt.description: “Heat-vulnerable” parts of the city have few trees, little shade and limited access to air-conditioning. And the risk of death is also higher.

nyt.title: See How Europe’s Heat Waves Melted the Alps’ Glaciers
nyt.description: The snowfall from last winter disappeared a month sooner than usual, after two early hot spells. Huge volumes of exposed ice are now starting to vanish.

nyt.title: Tucker Carlson, Who Broke With Trump, Plans to ‘Help Build a Third Party’
nyt.description: The influential conservative commentator’s relationship with the president and the G.O.P. fractured over the war with Iran. Now, he says he is charting a new course.

nyt.title: Ocasio-Cortez Endorses Abdul El-Sayed in Crucial Michigan Senate Race
nyt.description: The endorsement is the first in a contested Senate primary by Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez this year, in a state that Democrats believe they must hold this fall to win a Senate majority.

nyt.title: Ukraine escalates military pressure on Russian-held Crimea
nyt.description: Escalating drone strikes, fuel shortages and power cuts in the region Russia annexed are among the factors turning up the heat on President Vladimir V. Putin.

nyt.title: Russia Bombards Ukrainian Capital With Deadly Wave of Attacks
nyt.description: At least 27 people were killed in drone and missile strikes on Kyiv that damaged several residential buildings across the city, the authorities said.

nyt.title: Even as It Bombards Kyiv, Russia’s Wider Military Campaign Has Largely Stalled
nyt.description: Moscow can still inflict serious damage, but its forces are suffering higher casualties than their Ukrainian counterparts, analysts say.

nyt.title: David Hearn, Olympian Canoeist, Is Indicted After Arrest at Trump’s Reflecting Pool
nyt.description: David Hearn, a former canoeist, is accused of vandalizing the algae-challenged pool, which President Trump has said he would repair and beautify with fresh sealant. But the algae returned and the paint peeled.

nyt.title: Trump-Linked Firm’s Fees for Organizing Freedom 250 Events Remain Secret
nyt.description: Event Strategies, Inc., a longtime vendor to President Trump’s campaigns, is organizing the Great American State Fair and the July 4 celebrations.

nyt.title: JD Vance and Melania Trump Also Had Sharp Earnings Increases in 2025
nyt.description: But the revenue brought in by the vice president and the first lady paled in comparison to that of President Trump.

nyt.title: U.S. Officials Believed Israel Was Plotting to Kill Iranian Negotiators
nyt.description: Any Israeli attempt to kill Abbas Araghchi, the foreign minister, or Mohammad Ghalibaf, the Parliament speaker, would have derailed peace talks, American officials feared.

nyt.title: Man Rescued 8 Days After Quake, a Ray of Joy in Stricken Venezuela
nyt.description: The 44-year-old security guard was pulled alive from a pancaked basement, offering a fleeting moment of hope amid a soaring death toll.

nyt.title: An Aerial View of Disaster at a Venezuela Housing Project
nyt.description: What one aerial image of a collapsed building tells us about the aftermath of an earthquake in La Guaira, Venezuela.

nyt.title: A ‘Muslims Only’ Swim Party and the Backlash That Followed
nyt.description: A Muslim mother’s plan for an Eid swim party near Dallas drew backlash, then threats that upended her quiet life.

nyt.title: Less Than 10 Percent of Eligible Children Have Trump Accounts
nyt.description: More than six million have been signed up for the investment accounts, which open for contributions July 4, but there are barriers to uptake.

nyt.title: Black Soldiers In the Revolutionary War: A New England Journey
nyt.description: Across New England, a writer traveled down dirt paths and into historic homes to find the forgotten stories of the enslaved men who fought for freedom on two fronts.

nyt.title: How to Make a Time Capsule That Will Last 250 Years
nyt.description: The America250 time capsule will hold dozens of historical treasures. Avoiding dampness and other dangers requires lots of engineering.

nyt.title: In Tumultuous Term, Chief Justice Roberts Took Charge of Unruly Supreme Court
nyt.description: The chief justice faced down the president, forged unlikely coalitions and achieved long-sought goals.

npr.title: Are the wars in Ukraine and Iran showing the limits of global powers?
npr.description: We look at the Russian attacks on Kyiv and the overall state of the wars between Russia and Ukraine and the U.S. and Iran.

npr.title: Trump denies conflict of interest over crypto. And, Vatican excommunicates rebel group
npr.description: Trump and his family earned over $1 billion last year through cryptocurrency ventures and other businesses. And, the Vatican declared that the traditionalist Society of St. Pius X has entered schism.

npr.title: Former ethics lawyer says Trump's crypto poses 'clear conflict of interest'
npr.description: Former White House ethics lawyer Richard Painter says President Trump "stands alone" in having substantial financial conflicts of interest and that, "for every other executive branch official, it would be a violation."

npr.title: Vatican declares Society of St. Pius X in schism, excommunicates bishops
npr.description: The Vatican responded Thursday to a traditionalist society that consecrated bishops without the pope's consent, declaring the Society of St. Pius X in schism and excommunicating its bishops and priests.

npr.title: Russia hits Ukraine's capital with a massive drone and missile attack, killing at least 18
npr.description: Russia launched a large-scale attack on Ukraine's capital overnight into Thursday, with ballistic and cruise missiles and drones, killing several people.

npr.title: U.S. and Iran hold separate meetings in Qatar and agree to continue discussions
npr.description: U.S. and Iranian negotiators met separately on Wednesday with Qatari and Pakistani mediators, with "positive progress made," and they agreed to continue discussions, host Qatar said.

npr.title: A major Russian attack kills 17 in Kyiv as Ukraine keeps striking Moscow's oil sector
npr.description: Loud explosions shook Kyiv for hours during the night, with many people sheltering at subway stations. Emergency crews were digging through the rubble of collapsed buildings in search of victims.

npr.title: Untold casualties and humanitarian needs: What to know a week from Venezuela's quakes
npr.description: Here's a look at some of the major developments since major back-to-back earthquakes rocked Venezuela on June 24, devastating parts of a country already reeling from crisis after crisis.

npr.title: Funerals held for 14 Pakistani children killed in tutoring center collapse
npr.description: Police are investigating whether negligence during construction work caused the collapse in the eastern city of Lahore on Tuesday.

npr.title: Greetings from London, where Banksy's flag man is a warning cry
npr.description: As he marches on, his flag blows back into his face, leaving him unaware he is only a step away from a perilous fall. As usual with Banksy's art, the statue presents a sharp critique of society.

republika.title: Strage di Altavilla, ergastolo per Barreca e la coppia diabolica
republika.description: Al padre e marito delle tre vittime non riconosciuto lo sconto per la semi infermità mentale. Fina e Carandente i registi della mattanza nella villa

republika.title: Trump proclama la Giornata nazionale delle capesante. “Se votate i comunisti non le potrete più pescare”
republika.description: L’annuncio su Truth del presidente americano. La mossa, in vista delle elezioni di midterm, per festeggiare un provvedimento che apre alla pesca dei molluschi nel New England

Palinsesti Rai, il valzer dei conduttori. Ma che fatica trovare le novità
republika.description: Tra poche ore la presentazione di quel che vedremo nella prossima stagione. Restano il nodo di “Chi l’ha visto?” e le perplessità su Monteleone. Tra i pochi debutti quello di Brumotti

republika.title: Almaviva, il giovane “scelto” da Totti non è più un giocatore della Roma
republika.description: Il contratto con il club giallorosso non è stato rinnovato. Il messaggio social del giovane è commovente: "Difficile trovare le parole giuste”

republika.title: Nanni Moretti verso Venezia? Intanto un corto delizioso e un annuncio: “Il film esce a dicembre”
republika.description: Videomessaggio agli esercenti riuniti a Riccione per “Succederà questa notte”, l’atteso nuovo lavoro del regista che potrebbe essere alla Mostra del cinema

republika.title: Covid, dal governo 100 milioni all’azienda dell’imprenditore vicino a FdI. L’opposizione attacca
republika.description: Schillaci in Senato conferma la transazione con JC Electronics conclusa dopo che la società ha vinto una causa in primo grado per un mancato appalto per mascherine. Pd e 5stelle: “Perché questo regalo prima dell’appello?”

republika.title: I ministri alla festa americana: “Occorre pari dignità, sulla difesa decidiamo noi”
republika.description:
Dopo le accuse di Trump, vicepremier e esponenti di governo per l’Independence
day a Villa Taverna. Meloni assente, c’è la sorella Arianna: “Le stoccate del tycoon
non ci fanno effetto”

republika.title: Monaco, svolta nell'attentato all'oligarca: “L'autrice è una donna ucraina”
republika.description: Fonti a conoscenza delle indagini hanno rivelato a Le Figaro che il responsabile dell’attacco all’oligarca Ermolaev non sarebbe un uomo come sospettato all’inizio

republika.title: Wimbledon, Tien si sente male in campo e mangia pane. Va in ospedale e ordina hamburger e pollo fritto
republika.description: Un dolore allo stomaco lo costringe a prendersi una pausa. Dopo la sconfitta è costretto a ricoverarsi, ma la sua alimentazione non è esattamente salutare

republika.title: Meloni alla Uil: “Morti sul lavoro una sconfitta per tutti”
republika.description: La premier a Padova al congresso nazionale della confederazione: “Tolleranza zero sul caporalato”

republika.title: Mille giorni dal 7 ottobre, proteste anti-Netanyahu in Israele: “La verità è stata sepolta”
republika.description: A Tel Aviv manifestazioni per chiedere un’inchiesta sul fallimento del governo nel prevenire l’attacco

republika.title: Il drone killer che immortala le vittime
republika.description: La nuova frontiera dell'orrore: robot assassini fissano i volti dei soldati nell'attimo in cui capiscono di essere condannati

republika.title: Schlein presenta la ricetta dem alla Federmanager: “Oggi parlo di crescita”
republika.description: Superamento dell’unanimità in Europa, questione salariale e occupazione femminile, le proposte dei dem

republika.title: “Come mille giorni di guerra a Gaza hanno consumato i nostri corpi e i nostri cuori”

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

phys-org.title: Brown leaves before fall could signal lasting heat damage, researchers warn
phys-org.description: Due to increasing heat and drought, forests are turning brown more often before autumn, when leaf senescence normally occurs. It is often unclear whether the trees are actively shedding foliage to avoid a breakdown in water transport or whether browning leaves are a consequence of irreversible damage caused by both heat and drought. As a result, the resilience of forests to climate extremes could be overestimated, WSL researchers warn in a recent commentary.

phys-org.title: Compromise drives shared risky decisions, but biased blame and credit can break teamwork
phys-org.description: Relationships are all about compromise. From deciding on where to eat dinner with a friend to negotiating chore lists at home, we often experience situations that require some flexibility. But what happens when we must work with others—especially people we don't know—to make a risky decision? That's what Caltech's Dean Mobbs, professor of cognitive neuroscience, and members of his lab set out to explore in a recent study.

phys-org.description: The transmission of optical information through random scattering media is a major challenge in optics, biomedical imaging, telecommunications and remote sensing. When light passes through a turbid or diffusive medium, such as biological tissue or a randomly structured optical material, the original image information can be severely distorted, making reliable recovery difficult.

phys-org.title: More gray seals counted in the Wadden Sea

During the 2025–2026 survey year, 3,385 pups and 12,497 gray seals were recorded during the molting period. The results have been published in the report "Grey Seal Numbers of the Wadden Sea and Helgoland 2025–2026," available on Zenodo.

The paper is published in Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Prescribed burns may generate over 20% of fine particle pollution in southeastern US
phys-org.description: Prescribed fires are vital for reducing wildfire risk and sustaining forest biodiversity. But they also contribute significantly to air pollution and smoke exposure, according to new research from the University of Georgia. The issue is especially pertinent to the southeastern United States, where 60% of all prescribed fires in the country occur. More than 20% of the fine-particle pollution in the southeastern U.S. can be attributed to prescribed burns, the study found.

phys-org.title: How to stop a mouse plague
phys-org.description: The scenes are biblical. Tens of thousands of rodents scattering across canola fields, behind sheds, into machinery. River fish with bellies full of mice. Carcasses littering the street, the sidewalk, outside your home. In supermarkets, the inescapable stench of dead and dying mice. These are the undeniable signs of a mouse plague.

phys-org.title: Light flips bacterial signaling enzyme between two shapes, unlocking how signals travel
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Bayreuth and Forschungszentrum Jülich have demonstrated that specific light-sensitive enzymes—so-called sensor histidine kinases (SHKs)—transmit their signal through a light-controlled change in asymmetry. With their new study, the researchers contribute to a better understanding of a central mechanism of bacterial signal processing. This may help develop new tools for biomedicine or biotechnology. The findings are reported in the journal Science Advances.

phys-org.title: AI analysis of data from multiple sensors can improve earthquake detection
phys-org.description: One seismometer is often not enough to reliably detect earthquakes or human activity such as underground nuclear tests. Rather, researchers combine readings from seismometers distributed across a small geographic area to gain confidence in their analysis. Artificial intelligence (AI) can combine readings from multiple sensors more effectively than classic technology, enabling more reliable detection of weak seismic signals, a new study by A. Köhler and colleagues shows.

phys-org.title: The broader a fungus's diet, the better it kills insects and helps plants
phys-org.description: Many fungi lead triple lives—acting as deadly insect pathogens, decomposers in the soil, and helpful partners living inside and transferring insect-derived nitrogen to plant roots. Scientists have long wondered what allows a single species to pull off these very different roles.

phys-org.title: Spontaneous current loops in a kagome metal point to hidden quantum order
phys-org.description: Quantum materials, materials exhibiting physical behavior governed by the laws of quantum mechanics, have proved promising for the development of numerous advanced technologies, including quantum technologies, memory devices and solar panels. In some of these materials, electrons can collectively arrange themselves in unusual patterns, giving rise to states that cannot be explained by classical physics theories.

phys-org.description: Two-dimensional (2D) perovskites are increasingly recognized as promising candidate materials for the next generation of optoelectronic devices. These materials combine key characteristics of both 2D semiconductors and three-dimensional (3D) perovskites.

proj-syn.title: 250 Years of American State Capitalism
proj-syn.description: While the prevailing economic narrative in the United States has often extolled free markets, policymaking itself has always been more pragmatic. From its very founding, the US has had a hybrid model in which the state directs, subsidizes, and occasionally bails out private enterprise in the service of national priorities.

proj-syn.title: Three Essentials of a More Equal World Order
proj-syn.description: A growing awareness of the inequities embedded in the world order has prompted calls for reform. Building a multilateral system that serves the global majority will require redesigning the international financial architecture, especially in relation to sovereign debt and corporate taxation.

proj-syn.title: The US as the World’s Robber Baron
proj-syn.description: Like the Gilded Age robber barons, the United States under President Donald Trump is using trade policy to benefit itself at the expense of all other countries. But now that administration surrogates are openly acknowledging the strategy, all other major trading powers will surely respond accordingly.

proj-syn.title: A Democratic Opening for Azerbaijan
proj-syn.description: With Armenia's recent elections likely to usher in an era of greater stability—and less Russian influence—in the South Caucasus, neighboring Azerbaijan is well-positioned to deepen cooperation with the US and Europe. But without appropriate conditions, new strategic partnerships with the West could fail to deliver for Azerbaijanis.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Europe’s Economy
proj-syn.description: While Nobel laureate economists Paul Krugman and Philippe Aghion disagree over how to measure Europe’s productivity gap with the United States, both overlook the value of its accumulated assets. That blind spot obscures the real story: Europe is living off a remarkable inheritance it has yet to convert into new growth.

proj-syn.title: NATO Needs a Defense Market
proj-syn.description: To convert NATO members' resources into military capabilities, setting defense as a strategic priority, increasing spending, and improving procurement systems are all steps in the right direction. But member countries will need to expand their industrial capacity—and that requires much more.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Choices Shaping our Children’s Health
proj-syn.description: Around the world, childhood is being reprogrammed by digital technologies that shape how young people learn, play, and connect. But children and young people are not experimental subjects, a captive market, or a commodity, which is why we must shape digital environments that protect and support their healthy development.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchy’s Ancient Origins
proj-syn.description: The struggle between democracy and oligarchy in classical Greece was bitter, with oligarchies relying on skillfully designed political institutions to shore up unpopular regimes. As concerns grow over the “rule of the few” in the United States, Americans should consider how their own institutions are doing oligarchs’ work for them.

proj-syn.title: How Modi Has Remade India
proj-syn.description: Over the last 12 years, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has overseen dizzying progress in economic modernization and state capacity-building, as well as dismaying setbacks on institutional independence and minority inclusion. This record offers important insights into how India will navigate the 21st century.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Trap
proj-syn.description: Policymakers obsessed with competitiveness both in Europe and beyond need to abandon old orthodoxies. New research finds that for two decades, capital in Europe has been abundant and cheap, and corporate profits strong, yet investment, productivity, and wages have stalled, and labor's share of total income has shrunk.

proj-syn.title: How to Empower Africa’s Multilateral Development Banks
proj-syn.description: Capitalizing multilateral development banks in Africa is a strategic investment in the continent’s economic transformation. To mobilize adequate funding will require leveraging domestic savings, pursuing monetary integration, using innovative financing mechanisms, and strengthening regional capital markets.

proj-syn.title: Why Americans Are Wary of AI
proj-syn.description: The tech industry is asking Americans to embrace AI at a moment when trust in government is declining. While these may seem like separate issues, persuading people to trust AI will be far more difficult if they do not trust the institutions responsible for regulating it.

proj-syn.title: Why the Gulf Needs Economic Ties with Iran
proj-syn.description: Most Gulf observers agree that the old security order is dying. But none of the most commonly proposed options—buying more advanced weapons, seeking protection from new partners in the Global South, or building stronger national militaries—is sufficient on its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Way to Tackle Developing Countries’ Cancer Crisis
proj-syn.description: Some health advocates believe that weakening intellectual-property protections and capping prices for the most advanced cancer treatments would expand access in developing countries. But this well-intentioned argument overlooks an inescapable reality: without strong incentives for innovation, such treatments would not exist.

proj-syn.title: Enforce AI Guardrails Before It’s Too Late
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration’s decision to impose export controls on Anthropic’s latest models is emblematic of the incoherent and shifting response from policymakers worldwide to the rapidly advancing AI sector. To ensure that these tools do not court disaster, governments must establish meaningful guardrails.

proj-syn.title: Is a European Single Market for Energy Such a Good Idea?
proj-syn.description: Although textbook microeconomics shows why less energy-market fragmentation would be better for Europe as a whole, that does not mean it would be a good deal for countries producing low-carbon electricity at minimal marginal cost. In fact, if more integration creates free riders, the political backlash could be profound.
